title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's 'Questions sur V.A. et groupes formels' (c. 1966, Tate/crystals dossier). Question 1, from Barsotti, asks: if two abelian varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p have isogenous formal groups, are the abelian varieties isogenous? On the previous page Grothendieck sets up a negative answer when the 'hypersingular' (p-rank 0) hypothesis is dropped. He takes dimension 2 and the formal type \hat G_m x G_{1,1}, i.e. p-rank 1. By Manin, Jacobians of this type form a 2-dimensional family N inside the 3-dimensional moduli M_2. He then claims that the non-simple members, those isogenous to E x F with E ordinary and F supersingular, form a family of dimension at most 1.

This page justifies that claim and finishes the counterexample.
(i) 'N.B. There is no continuous family of varieties isogenous to E x F.' More precisely he asserts that every abelian surface isogenous to E x F (over an algebraically closed field) is isomorphic to a product E' x F'. Hence, he says, the non-simple locus is a closed subfamily of N. It is the image of the open set M' of ordinary curves in the modular curve M under E -> E x F, with F running over the finitely many supersingular j-invariants.
(ii) If A is simple with this fixed formal structure, the A' isogenous to A form a discrete (countable, though infinite) set. Precisely: if A is defined over k, every A' is defined over a finite extension of k. The reason is that the local-local part G_{1,1} has a-number 1, so it has only a finite chain of subgroup schemes of each order. There are therefore no continuous families of infinitesimal quotients.
(iii) Consequently the transcendence degree over F_p of a field of definition (equivalently, of the moduli point) is an isogeny invariant within this stratum. Take points of the simple locus U in N with different transcendence degrees (0, 1, 2 are possible, since dim N = 2). These give simple abelian surfaces with isomorphic formal groups \hat G_m x G_{1,1} that are not isogenous. So Barsotti's question has a negative answer outside the supersingular case.

The argument is essentially the countability of isogeny classes (Hecke orbits) in strata where the a-number is at most 1, combined with a dimension or transcendence count.
errors: Claim (i) is false as stated. Take E ordinary and F supersingular, so Hom(E,F)=0, and let A=(E x F)/Gamma, with Gamma the graph of an isomorphism E[n] -> F[n] where (n,p)=1. Then A is isogenous to E x F but is not a product. Its only elliptic subvarieties are the images of E and F, and these meet in a group isomorphic to E[n], not in 0. (Over C, such gluings give Jacobians of genus-2 curves; cf. Kani.)

Consequently the non-simple locus in N is not just the image of finitely many curves E -> E x F. It is a countable union of 1-dimensional loci, one for each gluing datum. The conclusion 'dimension at most 1' and the final argument survive, because the simple locus still contains points of transcendence degree 2 and the countability within an isogeny class still holds.

The discreteness in (ii) relies on the a-number being at most 1 (formal type \hat G_m x G_{1,1}). It would fail for supersingular surfaces (Moret-Bailly families of alpha_p-quotients). This fits Grothendieck's restriction to the non-hypersingular case but is not made explicit on the page.

ideas.what: Abelian surfaces isogenous to E x F with Hom(E,F)=0 are claimed to be products (no continuous family in an isogeny class)
ideas.modern_name: Which abelian surfaces are products of elliptic curves; gluing (E x F)/graph of an isomorphism on E[n]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oort (Math. Ann. 1975); Kani for gluing constructions

ideas.what: Isogeny class of an abelian variety with a-number 1 (fixed formal type) is countable; isogenous varieties are defined over finite extensions of each other's fields of definition
ideas.modern_name: Countability of Hecke orbits / isogeny leaves being 0-dimensional when a<=1 (Oort foliation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oort (Foliations in moduli spaces of abelian varieties, 2004), building on folklore

ideas.what: Transcendence degree of the moduli point as an isogeny invariant, used to produce non-isogenous simple abelian surfaces with the same formal group (negative answer to Barsotti's question outside the supersingular case)
ideas.modern_name: Formal group (p-divisible group / Newton polygon) does not determine the isogeny class; central-leaf versus isogeny-leaf dimensions

missed.claim: As early as 1966 Grothendieck formulates the principle that, in a stratum with fixed formal group of a-number 1, isogeny classes are discrete, so transcendence degree is an isogeny invariant. This is an embryonic form of Oort's later isogeny-leaf / central-leaf dichotomy. He uses it to answer Barsotti's question negatively in the non-supersingular case.
missed.quote: les A' isogènes à A forment une famille discrète, (bien qu'infinie), de façon précise si A est définissable sur k, alors les A' sont définissables sur une extension finie de k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority only; the mathematics is now standard via Oort's foliation theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, fairly elementary dimension/countability argument, and it is now standard. One supporting claim (that every surface isogenous to E x F is a product) is wrong, though the conclusion survives. Its interest is mainly historical, as an early sketch of ideas later systematized by Oort.
transcription_corrections: 'toute courbe [?] isogène à E×F' should probably read 'toute variété isogène à E×F'.
'sous-famille fermée [?] de $E$' should read 'sous-famille fermée de $N$'.
'formé de celles qui sont ordinaires' refers to the ordinary elliptic curves forming the open set M' of M.

The struck line reads approximately '[soit] U dans N formé des variétés simples'. In the margin, 'UcN' is U ⊂ N: 'Si on prend des points de U ⊂ N distincts ayant des degrés de transcendance distincts'.
The final formal type should be \hat G_m × G_{1,1} (p-rank 1, matching the previous page's \hat G_{1,0} + G_{1,1}), not '$\overline{G}_{1,1}\times G_{1,1}$'.
